details.summary: A smart, fast weeknight soup that cleverly uses white beans instead of cream and frozen squash to save time. However, requiring a massive half-cup of cold Greek yogurt as a garnish per bowl will ruin the temperature and texture of the soup; the yogurt must be blended smoothly into the pot off-heat, and minor reductions to the squash and salt are needed to hit the chapter's macro limits.

dimensions.feedback: Sage, butternut squash, and white beans form a classic, coherent flavor profile, nicely anchored by the savory garlic and onion powders.
Every ingredient listed in the ingredients section is correctly utilized in the instructions.
Cook times are given as ranges, a check time is provided, and excellent visual cues ('shimmering', 'completely tender', 'velvety and completely smooth') guide the reader.
The ingredients and pureed soup format perfectly match a Modern American soup profile.
Simmering pre-diced frozen squash until tender and pureeing with beans is a highly reliable and rapid method for achieving a creamy texture.
The computed nutrition values align logically with the specified quantities of squash, beans, and Greek yogurt.
The title is fully accurate, and the intro highlights the culinary mechanics (bean puree for creaminess) and convenience without resorting to banned health claims.

Swirling a full 1/2 cup (113g) of cold, thick Greek yogurt into a single bowl of hot soup as a garnish is a culinary flaw—it will drastically cool the soup and clump rather than swirl elegantly. To keep the protein high without ruining the eating experience, direct the reader to blend or whisk the yogurt directly into the warm pot (off the heat) before ladling.
An excellent example of Mediterranean principles applied to American flavors, using high-fiber legumes and vegetables for a creamy texture instead of saturated fat.
Zero added sugars, and the carbohydrate load is sourced entirely from high-quality, fiber-rich whole foods (squash and beans).

Escalating the automated warnings: The recipe overshoots both the sodium and carbohydrate ceilings for a 'Light Main'. details.summary: A fantastic, genuinely fast weeknight soup that makes smart, realistic use of everyday shortcuts like frozen squash and canned beans. However, whisking a large volume of nonfat Greek yogurt into the hot broth will curdle and make the soup far too sour; reducing the yogurt and moving it to a garnish will perfect the recipe.

dimensions.feedback: Using 8 oz (a full half-cup per serving) of Greek yogurt, plus apple cider vinegar, will make this soup overwhelmingly tart and mask the delicate flavors of the butternut squash and sage. Reduce the yogurt to 2 to 4 oz total and omit the apple cider vinegar entirely.
